proposals.name: Mason County Eastern District Operating Millage Proposal
proposals.description:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law. The school district is required to levy 18 mills for operating purposes to receive its full revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Mason County Eastern…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law. The school district is required to levy 18 mills for operating purposes to receive its full revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Mason County Eastern District, Mason, Lake and Manistee Counties, Michigan, be increased by 6 mills ($6.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 8 years, 2026 to 2033, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 0.1474 mill of the 6 mills is levied in 2026 is approximately $19,378 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?
proposals.officialTitle: MASON COUNTY EASTERN DISTRICT OPERATING MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 18 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all…
proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its full revenue per pupil foundation allowance and restores millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963.
Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Manistee Area Public Schools, Manistee and Mason Counties, Michigan, be renewed by 18.5593 mills ($18.5593 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 4 years, 2027 to 2030, inclusive, and also be increased by .5000 mill ($0.5000 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 4 years, 2027 to 2030, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 18 mills are levied in 2027 is approximately $5,571,456 (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2026 levy and the addition of millage which will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963)?
proposals.officialTitle: MANISTEE AREA PUBLIC SCHOOLS OPERATING MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote continues the existing levy of 18 mills for 4 years — generally no increase over what you pay now, plus the restored or added amount described.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote lets the current millage expire; the service it funds would need cuts or other revenue.
proposals.conservativeView: Renewals are the least disruptive way to keep a service funded, but every renewal is a chance to ask whether the service is delivering value. Watch for "renewal" proposals that quietly restore Headlee rollbacks — that is a tax increase.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law. The school district is required to levy 18 mills for operating purposes to receive its full revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Mason County Eastern District, Mason, Lake and Manistee Counties, Michigan, be increased by 6 mills ($6.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 8 years, 2026 to 2033, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 0.1474 mill of the 6 mills is levied in 2026 is approximately $19,378 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?
proposals.officialTitle: MASON COUNTY EASTERN DISTRICT OPERATING MILLAGE PROPOSAL

proposals.ballotLanguage: Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Mason County Eastern District, Mason, Lake and Manistee Counties, Michigan, be increased by and the board of education be authorized to levy not to exceed 0.0511 mill ($0.0511 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 3 years, 2026, 2027 and 2028, for sinking fund purposes, including for school security improvements; for the acquisition or upgrading of technology; for the construction or repair of school buildings; for the purchase of real estate for school sites; for the acquisition of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used for the maintenance of student transportation vehicles; for the acquisition of eligible trucks and vans used to carry parts, equipment, and personnel for or in the maintenance of school buildings; for the acquisition of parts, supplies, and equipment used to maintain such trucks and vans; and for all other purposes authorized by law; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2026 is approximately $14,919 (this millage is to restore millage for sinking fund purposes lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963)?
proposals.officialTitle: MASON COUNTY EASTERN DISTRICT SINKING FUND MILLAGE PROPOSAL
proposals.yesVote: A YES vote raises the levy back to the originally authorized 0.0511 mills, overriding the Headlee Amendment rollback — this is a tax increase over the current rate.
proposals.noVote: A NO vote keeps the current, rolled-back rate in place.
proposals.conservativeView: The Headlee Amendment is a constitutional taxpayer protection that limits how fast property-tax revenue can grow. Overriding it raises taxes above what the constitution would otherwise allow.
proposals.progressiveView: Restores funding that inflation and Headlee rollbacks have eroded so existing services can continue.

The school district is required to levy 18 mills for operating purposes to receive its full revenue per pupil foundation allowance.

proposals.ballotLanguage:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law. The school district is required to levy 18 mills for operating purposes to receive its full revenue per pupil foundation allowance.
Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Mason County Eastern District, Mason, Lake and Manistee Counties, Michigan, be increased by 6 mills ($6.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 8 years, 2026 to 2033, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 0.1474 mill of the 6 mills is levied in 2026 is approximately $19,378 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?
